case_study_insert.main_stem: Northstar Software (NSD) is a private limited company in the software sector, employing a workforce of 60. Founded in 2011 by Priya Raman, it develops cloud accounting software for small firms and operates a flat structure with democratic leadership. NSD plans to invest $900,000 in a new cloud data centre with automated testing tools, financed by a $600,000 ten-year bank loan and $300,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $420,000 a year, a variable cost of $14.00 a unit and a selling price of $29.00, and currently produces 80,000 units a year. NSD faces two problems: labour turnover has reached 14% and a skills gap in cloud engineering is slowing product releases.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Quality and Operations Report — Q4 2025: NSD released 18,000 software licences last quarter; the test log recorded a defect rate of 2.4%, down from 4.6% a year earlier. Customer support tickets fell from 310 to 185 per month. Average resolution time is 6.5 hours. A survey of 450 business clients found 68% would pay 5% more for guaranteed 99.9% uptime, and 57% rate data security as their top purchasing criterion. A skills audit shows 22 of 60 staff have not completed training on the new cloud platform; specialist external training costs $1,200 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Northstar Software for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Technology Bulletin (January 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 4.25% to 5.0%, increasing borrowing costs for firms with variable-rate loans. (2) Average salaries for qualified software developers rose by 8.5%, pushing up wage bills across the technology sector. (3) Wholesale cloud-server and data-storage input costs rose 11.0% year-on-year, while business software spending grew 4.2% over the same period.

questions.question_text: NSD plans to fund part of its $900,000 cloud data centre with a bank loan. Explain two advantages for NSD of using retained profit instead of the bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Using retained profit costs NSD no interest charges or repayments, protecting cash flow while it services a $600,000 bank loan and funds the $900,000 cloud data centre. Every dollar saved on interest can be spent on specialist training at $1,200 per employee to close the skills gap and reduce 14% labour turnover, or absorbed if cloud-server input costs rise 11.0%. Keeping the $300,000 in-house also means the 80,000-unit software licence output does not have to carry extra debt service.

Point 2: Retained profit carries no collateral risk. If the new data centre failed to attract customers, a lender could call in the $600,000 loan, whereas $300,000 of internal funds puts no company asset at risk and preserves Priya Raman's control. It also avoids lender conditions on how the automated testing tools are introduced, letting NSD respond flexibly to the 2.4% defect rate and the 68% of surveyed clients who want guaranteed uptime. Retained profit is therefore cheaper, safer and leaves decisions with the founder.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to NSD's financing decision, costs and expansion.

questions.question_text: NSD is launching a new cloud accounting package. Consider advertising in the national business press, paid search and social media advertising, or sponsoring a technology trade conference. Which should NSD choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
National business press advertising: Full-page ads in national business newspapers would build credibility and reach owners of small firms, the target market for NSD's cloud accounting software. However, airtime and design costs are high, much of the readership is outside the small-firm segment, and the message is one-way with no click-through data. For a 60-person company already committing $900,000 to a data centre and servicing a $600,000 loan, this broad, expensive reach would waste scarce cash.

Paid search and social media advertising: These channels reach people actively searching for accounting software and can be targeted at small-firm decision-makers, with measurable clicks and low entry cost. They suit a product whose 68% of surveyed clients already want 99.9% uptime and 57% rank data security first, because copy can highlight those features directly and be adjusted quickly using ticket data (310 down to 185 per month). The drawback is that costs rise with competition for keywords and results need skilled management NSD currently lacks given its cloud-engineering skills gap.

Technology trade conference sponsorship: This puts NSD in front of an audience of IT professionals and partners, generating high-quality leads and demonstration opportunities for automated testing. It is far cheaper than a national press campaign but reaches few small-firm buyers directly, so the 80,000-unit sales target would not be supported, and one event gives only a short-lived spike.

Recommendation: NSD should choose paid search and social media advertising. It is measurable, affordable and targets the exact clients in its 450-person research who value security and uptime. National press is rejected as expensive and untargeted; conference sponsorship is rejected as too narrow to drive 80,000 units. NSD should fund it from the $300,000 retained profit rather than adding debt.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Lists or describes promotional options with limited application to NSD.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discusses advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in NSD's context with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three options in NSD's context and gives a justified recommendation explaining why press advertising and conference sponsorship are rejected.

questions.question_text: NSD's labour turnover has reached 14% and it has a skills gap in cloud engineering. Explain two benefits for NSD of using democratic leadership to improve staff motivation.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership gives NSD's 60 employees a voice in how the new cloud data centre and automated testing tools are introduced. Consulting the engineers who handle releases satisfies social and esteem needs (Maslow) and makes staff feel valued, which directly targets the 14% labour turnover. When developers help set testing routines, they are more likely to stay, keeping the knowledge needed to cut the 2.4% defect rate and maintain 99.9% uptime promised to 68% of surveyed clients.

Point 2: Involvement generates practical ideas from the staff closest to the product, helping close the cloud-engineering skills gap without paying $1,200 per employee for every course. Participation is a motivator (Herzberg) that raises commitment and reduces the disruption caused when 22 of 60 staff still need training. In a flat structure with only a short chain of command, democratic decisions can be implemented quickly, protecting output of 80,000 units while the $900,000 expansion beds in.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to NSD's turnover, skills gap and expansion.

questions.question_text: NSD must train 22 staff who have not completed training on the new cloud platform. Consider on-the-job training or specialist external training at $1,200 per employee. Which should NSD choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Coaching at the workstation is specific to NSD's own cloud platform and automated testing tools, costs no external fees, and keeps the 22 staff productive while they learn, protecting output of 80,000 units and the drive to cut the 2.4% defect rate. Supervisors can demonstrate the exact release routines needed for 99.9% uptime. The drawback is that the trainers are themselves developers whose work slows down, bad habits can be copied, and there is no certificate, which may matter to the 57% of clients who rank data security as their top criterion.

Specialist external training: A college or vendor course gives structured, up-to-date cloud-engineering skills and a recognised qualification. For the 22 untrained staff the fee is 22 × $1,200 = $26,400, an explicit calculation from the insert figures and affordable against the $300,000 retained profit. It removes staff from releases temporarily and the generic content may not match NSD's exact platform, so follow-up coaching would still be needed, and 14% labour turnover raises the risk of losing newly trained staff.

Decision: NSD should choose on-the-job training first, with short external courses for the most senior engineers. On-the-job training is cheaper, platform-specific and avoids the $26,400 fee and loss of 22 staff from live releases while labour turnover is 14%. Full external training is rejected because the $26,400 cost and absence from the line would slow releases and the skills gap could return if trained staff leave. With 14% labour turnover the risk of losing newly qualified staff is real, so this blended approach limits that exposure while keeping the platform running.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to NSD.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of benefits and drawbacks of both methods in NSD's context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both methods with a justified decision covering cost, disruption and platform relevance, rejecting the alternative.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how NSD's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $420,000 ÷ ($29.00 − $14.00) = $420,000 ÷ $15.00 = 28,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 28,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $29.00 − $14.00 = $15.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $15.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways NSD's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare the 28,000-unit break-even output with actual output of 80,000 units to confirm a margin of safety of 52,000 units, showing how much sales can fall before losses occur while the $900,000 data centre is commissioned.
2. Use contribution of $15.00 to model discount offers to small firms: a $2.00 price cut would leave $13.00 contribution, so managers can see the extra unit volume needed to keep covering $420,000 fixed costs.
3. Check that 80,000 units × $15.00 = $1,200,000 contribution comfortably covers the $600,000 loan commitment and $420,000 fixed costs, informing whether further borrowing is safe.
4. Benchmark unit cost ($420,000 ÷ 80,000 = $5.25 plus $14.00 = $19.25 a unit) across quarters to spot rising support costs before the 11.0% cloud-server inflation arrives.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 28,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $15.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety of 52,000 units against 80,000-unit output; discount modelling with $420,000 fixed costs; loan-service feasibility on the $600,000 loan; and unit-cost benchmarking at $19.25 against input inflation.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method, 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate NSD's profitability by calculating the gross profit margin, profit margin and return on capital employed for 2024 and 2025. Has NSD's profitability improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 50.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 55.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 20.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 24.0%
ROCE 2024 = 18.0%
ROCE 2025 = 24.0%

Detailed workings: 2024 gross profit $900 ÷ revenue $1,800 = 50.0%; 2025 gross profit $1,320 ÷ revenue $2,400 = 55.0%. Operating profit 2024 $360 ÷ revenue $1,800 = 20.0%; 2025 $576 ÷ revenue $2,400 = 24.0%. Operating profit 2024 $360 ÷ capital employed $2,000 = 18.0%; 2025 $576 ÷ capital employed $2,400 = 24.0%. Revenue grew from $1,800 to $2,400 while cost of sales rose only from $900 to $1,080, so gross profit rose faster than sales.

Evaluation: Profitability strengthened across all three measures. The increased gross percentage shows better control of direct costs relative to sales, helped by a healthier spread between the $29.00 price and $14.00 variable cost. The operating percentage also rose because operating profit climbed from $360 to $576 faster than revenue, indicating fixed costs were spread over more output (80,000 units). The return on capital rose from 18.0% to 24.0%, so the $2,400 of capital employed is now working harder, which supports the case for the $900,000 data centre. Interest payable rose from $40 to $55, a small burden relative to $576 operating profit, though it signals higher borrowing.

Conclusion: NSD's profitability has clearly improved: all three measures rose together, and the rise is driven by revenue growth and cost control rather than by stripping out assets. The residual caution is that the higher interest charge and 14% labour turnover could erode the 24.0% return if the $600,000 loan is variable-rate, so margins must be defended.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE for both years with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years combined with detailed evaluation of revenue, cost and capital movements and a justified conclusion on profitability.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for NSD of introducing automated testing tools in its software development.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Automated testing tools directly attack the 2.4% defect rate recorded in NSD's test log, down from 4.6% a year earlier, by running consistent checks on every release. Fewer bugs mean support tickets stay below the current 185 per month and the 68% of surveyed clients who will pay 5% more for 99.9% uptime are more likely to be retained, protecting the $29.00 price and the $15.00 contribution on all 80,000 units.

Disadvantage: Buying and running the tools adds to the $900,000 data centre investment and may increase the $420,000 fixed costs, which would raise the 28,000-unit break-even output. It also needs cloud-engineering skills NSD lacks, with 22 of 60 staff untrained and 14% labour turnover, so staff resistance or misconfigured tests could initially increase defects and delay releases rather than reduce them. NSD can measure the effect against the 310 support tickets recorded before the improvement, so the investment is judged on evidence rather than assumption.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to NSD's defect rate, research data, costs and skills.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 5.0%, the 8.5% rise in developer salaries and the 11.0% rise in cloud-server input costs will affect NSD. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.25% to 5.0%): If NSD's $600,000 bank loan is variable-rate, the extra interest is 0.75% × $600,000 = $4,500 a year (0.0075 × $600,000). That is small beside $420,000 fixed costs and $576 of operating profit, and if the loan is fixed the effect is nil. Higher rates could also make future borrowing for the $900,000 data centre dearer, but NSD can cap this risk by fixing the rate.

Developer salary rise (8.5%): NSD employs a workforce of 60 and the insert does not state how many are developers or their hours, so no annual wage total can be invented. The honest judgement is qualitative: an 8.5% rise lifts unit labour cost unless productivity holds at 80,000 ÷ 60 = about 1,333 units per employee, and the existing skills gap and 14% labour turnover make this hard. It also makes the $1,200 external training fee relatively more attractive.

Cloud-server input cost inflation (11.0%): The insert gives a variable cost of $14.00 a unit but does not decompose it. A clearly labelled upper bound if the entire variable cost rose 11.0% is 0.11 × $14.00 = $1.54 a unit; across 80,000 units that is 80,000 × $1.54 = $123,200 a year, cutting contribution from $15.00 toward $13.46. Even a partial pass-through would materially shrink the surplus covering $420,000 fixed costs.

Conclusion: The 11.0% input-cost rise will have the greatest impact. It compounds on every unit, can add up to $123,200 a year on the stated assumptions and directly erodes the contribution that services the loan; the interest rise is only $4,500 at most and the wage effect cannot be quantified from the insert and can be offset by productivity.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external changes with limited application to NSD.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on NSD's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three changes in NSD's context with justified greatest-impact judgement and shown derivations, rejecting the smaller effects.
